featured_reviews.name: Amisha Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having visited countless seafood restaurants across Goa, the Konkan region, and Mumbai, I can confidently say that Jai Hind tops my list.

Yes, there’s almost always a long waiting line, and at times you may be asked to share a table with other diners. But honestly, that’s only because the place is packed with people who keep coming back for the food. And once you taste it, you’ll understand why.

The seafood is fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. What makes the experience even better is the value for money. Unlike many places that charge extra for every little thing, the thali here is genuinely generous and unlimited, you can ask for refills of the items in your thali as many times as you’d like.

Great food, excellent portions, and prices that feel justified. If you’re a seafood lover, the wait is absolutely worth it.

Jai Hind Lunch Home is honestly one of the BEST food spots for family dinners, celebrations, get-togethers, or even casual weekend meals. The food quality is consistently amazing, portions are generous, and the pricing is surprisingly affordable for the quantity and taste they serve.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Chaitanya for the second time, and it’s still one of the best places for authentic Konkan Malvani food in Dadar, Mumbai. Truly one of the rare restaurants that serves genuinely authentic seafood
Chaitanya easily ranks at the top!
The place is always crowded, so be prepared to wait outside for at least 20–40 minutes. The seating area is small, but the food makes it completely worth the wait. Prices depend on the current fish rates.
We tried the special prawns thali, which comes with double portions of prawns fry absolutely delicious. Also had the surmai thali with two fried pieces, and the taste was awesome. The bhakri was soft and fresh.
The best part was the unlimited solkadi, along with tasty crab lollipop. Service was quick too—food arrived within 5–10 minutes. Highly recommended for seafood lovers!

Along with that there was kaleji masala (liver gravy) one more fantastic preparation  of assal malvani food. Don't miss having it with kombdi wade(its made of traditional flour mixed and fried nice and fluffy) or ghavne (Rice flour). Along with this all, they will also serve Solkadi (its a drink made of nice blend of wild mangosteen fruits along with some garlic and coriander, its amazing drink) do not miss this.

And to conclued this tasty food have parole (made of Rice flour and grated coconut,sweetened by jaggery with lot of ghee)

You must visit to this place and do try the amazing food of Indian west costline. This place will not disappoint you at all..

The Fry Poplet was stuffed beautifully with a spicy, tangy masala that was bursting with flavor. Cooked to perfection with a nice crisp on the outside, it was one of my favorites.

The Fried Prawns were juicy, lightly coated, and seasoned just right — simple but full of flavor. And let’s not forget the Bombil Fry — soft on the inside, crispy on the outside, and absolutely fresh. It literally melts in your mouth!

The service was friendly and the ambience was clean and comfortable — nothing fancy, but perfect for a seafood feast. Highly recommend for anyone craving authentic, flavorful coastal food.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers!

The Food: Simply excellent. Every component of the thali—from the perfectly fried stuffed Pomfret with its crisp coating to the rich, flavorful coastal curry—tastes incredibly fresh and expertly spiced. It’s the kind of food that leaves you entirely satisfied yet already planning your next visit.
The Ambiance: The restaurant is small and cozy, but that’s exactly what gives it its charm. It has a genuinely warm, homely vibe that makes you feel instantly welcome, as if you're dining at a close friend's house.
Service & Staff: The service here is top-notch. The staff is exceptionally polite, courteous, and attentive, ensuring you have everything you need without ever feeling intrusive.
The Verdict: Incredible value for money! For the quality and quantity of food they serve, it is not expensive at all.
Highly recommended if you want spectacular coastal flavors paired with heartwarming hospitality. I will definitely be back for more!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an excellent meal at Maaslli and would highly recommend for local seafood lovers. We went for dinner a little before 8 and the place wasn't too full tho they do not have a lot of seating. The service was prompt, efficient and polite.

We ordered the paan style surmai that was wrapped in a banana leaf and roasted, the sukha bhujane prawns and the crab soup. -c. Bombil: 7/10

The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

A delightful meal at Flavors of Malvan in Prabhadevi! The food is exceptionally tasty, wholesome, and prepared in a way that feels truly home-style, yet packed with authentic coastal flavors.

The Green Chutney Surmai was outstanding, the Fish Curry with rice was comforting and flavorful, and the Koliwada Prawns were perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious. To top it all, the Kokum Soda was simply mind-blowing—refreshing, tangy, and the perfect accompaniment to the meal.

A special mention to Vinod and Navin, who were incredibly warm, welcoming, and attentive. They took the time to understand our preferences and suggested dishes that suited our tastes perfectly, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

If you're looking for authentic Malvani cuisine that combines traditional flavors with heartfelt hospitality, this place is a must-visit!The restaurant is Flavors of Malvan.

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Kasirajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was my daughter's birthday eve, and after some gentle persuasion to choose Pallavi's boutique café over Mumbai stalwarts like Trishna or Mahesh, we were seated in this beautifully done-up spot near Dadar's Shivaji Park. Though small, the space possesses a premium, fine-dining ambiance.

The Feast
Despite claiming to be "light eaters" (ahem!), we indulged in a vast selection, and every single dish was amazing. The true "Flavours" of Malwan shone through, outperforming many other seafood restaurants I've visited over the past 28 years (including Gajalee, Mahesh Lunch Home, and Sindhudurg).
Our order included:
	Refreshing Drinks: Sol Kadi, Kokum Soda, and Lemon Soda.
	Signature Seafood: Chutney Stuffed Pomfret Fry with Prawns, Chutney Stuffed Bombil Roll with Prawns, Sukka Crab, Tisrya Sukka, and Prawn Curry, paired with Rice Bhakri.
	Desserts: Ukdiche Modak and Puran Poli.

The Unforgettable Star
While every item was a feast for the taste buds, the Sukka Crab was the undisputed champion—absolutely outstanding! We literally wiped the plates clean and even drank the leftover Prawn Curry. This is food made with passion; food that truly leaves a lasting memory.

My words and photos simply cannot do full justice to the culinary magic at "Flavours of Malwan."

Don't just read about it—experience the authentic, soulful taste of Malwani cuisine for yourself!

Along with coastal specialties, the restaurant also offers a wide range of non-vegetarian options, including chicken and mutton dishes prepared with care and consistency. For those who prefer vegetarian food, Shashi Coastal Treat does not disappoint. Their Punjabi vegetarian dishes are rich, creamy, and full of authentic taste, making them a great choice for family dining.

In addition, the restaurant serves Chinese dishes that are flavorful and well-prepared, adding more variety to the menu and catering to diverse tastes. This balance between seafood, non-veg, and vegetarian cuisines makes Shashi Coastal Treat an ideal place for groups with mixed food preferences.

With its welcoming ambiance, quality service, and wide-ranging menu, Shashi Coastal Treat near Prabhadevi offers a complete dining experience. Whether you are craving coastal fish, Punjabi veg dishes, Chinese flavors, or classic non-veg meals, this restaurant delivers taste, quality, and satisfaction in every plate. 🍽️🐟

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavours Of China in Prabhadevi is a solid go-to spot for Indo-Chinese and Thai cuisine, especially if you’re looking for tasty food at reasonable pricing in the South Mumbai area.

🍽️ Food:
The food is definitely the highlight here. Their menu offers a wide variety—from classic Chinese gravies and noodles to Thai curries and rice. Dishes like burnt garlic rice, Manchurian, and Thai curries stand out for their bold flavours and generous portions. The taste is consistent, slightly on the Indianised side (which most people prefer), and perfect for comfort dining. Many customers also appreciate the freshness and customizable options available.

🥢 Portion Size & Value:
Portions are quite generous, making it ideal for sharing. Pricing is pocket-friendly for the quality and quantity offered, making it a great value-for-money option in the area.

🏠 Ambience:
The ambience is simple and casual—not a fine dining place, but clean and comfortable for a quick meal with friends or family. Seating space is slightly limited, so it can feel a bit cramped during peak hours.

🧑‍🍳 Service:
Service is generally quick, especially for takeaway and delivery orders. However, during busy hours, there can be slight delays and service could be more attentive.

📍 Location:
Conveniently located in Prabhadevi near Century Bazaar, it’s easily accessible and a popular neighbourhood dining spot.

⸻

✅ Pros:

* Delicious Indo-Chinese flavours
* Generous portion sizes
* Good value for money
* Wide menu variety (Chinese + Thai)

Horrible experience. I had come here to celebrate a special occasion with my senior citizen mother.

The AC was directly hitting our faces and food, so we politely requested the staff if they could just move the AC flap slightly upwards. We were simply told, “No, we can’t do it,” and the staff member walked away. I then requested another waiter, Mr. Mohan, who was serving us. He also refused and walked away. When I tried explaining the issue, he responded arrogantly, saying that they could not inconvenience other customers for one table.

When another table became vacant, I moved there to avoid creating any issue, but we were immediately stopped and told that the table was reserved. Even after that, Mr. Mohan continued arguing with us and grumbling, despite us sitting quietly and trying to enjoy our meal. It got to a point where I had no option but to leave.

What was most shocking was that the manager was standing right there throughout this entire incident and did absolutely nothing while his waiter was openly arguing with customers and raising his voice during dinner. Not once did he step in to de-escalate the situation or address our concern.

This was not just poor service it was complete disregard for customer comfort and basic respect, especially towards a senior citizen guest. A simple request was met with arrogance, hostility, and completely unprofessional behaviour.

I would request the concerned authorities and management to please look into this matter and take appropriate action, as no customer should have to go through such an experience.

This is a very popular Malavni & Kokani cuisine  restaurant  in Lalbaug area.
It is popular for its fresh seafood,Mutton & chicken dishes.
It follows thali system.

A Surmai orpomfret thali at around 1000/- however big the fish sounds too high so we had to skip them.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kokan Kinara Hotel

I recently visited Kokan Kinara Hotel with my family, and overall, it was a satisfying dining experience with a good variety of food options and reasonable pricing.

We started with Chicken Manchow Soup (₹120), which was thick, flavorful, and liked by everyone at the table. It was a good start to the meal. Next, we ordered Chicken Crispy, and the portion size really stood out—the pieces were bigger than what I usually get elsewhere, and the taste was quite good.

We then decided to try Chicken Lollipop in two styles to get some variety—half Dry (₹100) and half Gravy Masala (₹120), each with three pieces. Both versions tasted good, but personally, I would recommend the gravy version. It felt less oily, healthier, and the chicken was more tender compared to the fried dry version.

My father ordered the Komdi Vada Thali after seeing the menu photos. He was a bit disappointed because the chicken in the pictures looked boneless like kheema, but in reality, it was bone-in. Taste-wise, it was okay and filling. My mother wanted to try Crab Masala (₹250). Since it was difficult for her to eat comfortably at the restaurant, she requested it to be packed. Taste-wise, it was decent.

For the main course, my brother and I ordered Butter Chicken (₹190) with Butter Naan (₹50) and Chapatis (₹10 each). Compared to butter chicken we’ve tried at many other places, this one was okayish, not outstanding. My younger brother still wanted rice, so he ordered Chicken Fried Rice (half – ₹90), which was actually quite good.

We also ordered a Bisleri bottle (₹20), and the total bill came to ₹1550, which I feel is reasonable for the quantity and variety we ordered.

The ambience is decent, and there’s a fish tank with large fishes, which adds a nice touch. However, cleanliness could be improved. We were seated in a corner, and there was noticeable dust on the wall above us, which was uncomfortable.

Apart from that, the overall experience was good, and with a bit more focus on cleanliness and consistency in taste, the place could be even better.

featured_reviews.name: Paurnima Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Coast & Bloom at Dadar and it turned out to be a truly memorable dining experience that beautifully celebrates coastal and regional Indian flavors with a refined touch.

We began with the Lobster Thermidor, which was served in a rich, creamy mushroom sauce accompanied by sautéed vegetables, bread, and a perfectly cooked egg. The dish was indulgent, flavorful, and luxuriously satisfying. Alongside, we had the Tandoori Prawns, which carried an excellent smoky char from the tandoor. Paired with fresh green chutney and a sweet-tangy mango pickle, the combination elevated the entire starter experience.

For the main course, we opted for the Malvani Fish Curry with Ravas. The fish was exceptionally fresh, tender, and cooked to perfection, soaking beautifully in the aromatic Malvani gravy. We also tried the Chettinad Chicken, which had a bold, spicy profile and was packed with deep, authentic flavors.

To complement the curries, we had Malabar Parotta, Ghavane, and Chilli Cheese Garlic Naan. Each bread brought a different texture and paired wonderfully with the gravies, with the ghavane being a particularly delightful and unique accompaniment.

We also enjoyed Solkadi, which perfectly balanced the meal with its refreshing, lightly spiced tanginess. For drinks, we tried the Ratamba (kokum-based), Navy Punch, and Ginger Ale, all of which were refreshing and well-crafted.

To end the meal, we had the Crab Meat Fried Rice. While pleasant, this was comparatively simpler in flavor and had lesser crab meat than expected.

What truly stood out, beyond the food, was the exceptional service. The staff member assisting us went above and beyond — offering curry samples when we were confused between options and even showing us the raw fish to help us understand the portion and quality we would be served. Such thoughtful hospitality added immense value to the experience.

The entire meal came to ₹8,236, and considering the quality of ingredients, variety of dishes, and outstanding service, it felt well worth the price.

Coast & Bloom is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates coastal cuisine served with elegance, authenticity, and warm hospitality.

Thank you for such a detailed and thoughtful review! featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fish Curry Rice is a true celebration of coastal flavours and seafood mastery. Their seafood spread is outstanding — the surmai and pomfret are impeccably fresh, the halwa and bombil melt beautifully, and the fish fry along with the prawns curry are rich, fragrant, and deeply satisfying.

What truly stole the show were the tisrya sukka, mori masala, and kalva sukka — bold, soulful preparations that burst with authentic coastal character. The must-try list is long for a reason: prawns aluwadi, stuffed pomfret, bombil thecha fry, and chounak fry are each crafted with precision and irresistible flavour.

Their thalis deserve special praise — generous, well-balanced, and layered with flavour, offering a complete journey through coastal cuisine. A special mention to owner Sandesh Bhat — the heart and soul of FCR — who ensures taste and consistency are always bang on, and who, along with his attentive team, is always on his toes with spot-on recommendations tailored to your mood and palate.

A place where freshness meets finesse, and every plate tells a story of spice, sea, and tradition.

I visited The Big Fish & Co. on 4th January while I was shopping around Dadar with my mom and sister. While shopping nearby, we asked a local person for a good restaurant recommendation, and she suggested this place — and honestly, it turned out to be a great choice.
Right from the entrance, the experience was pleasant. The security guard at the door was very polite and kind. He asked if we had a reservation (we didn’t), but luckily a few tables were available. Since we were just three people, we were seated comfortably without any wait.
The ambience is quite good — warm, comfortable, and very suitable for families and friends. There were absolutely no negative points when it came to the atmosphere. What really touched my heart was the attentiveness of the staff. They listened carefully, were patient, and ensured everything was smooth. The service was quick, with no unnecessary delays, which I truly appreciated.
Coming to the food — it felt very local and authentic, something I personally connect with. The dishes were unique and well-prepared. We ordered tandoori prawns, which were medium-sized and nicely cooked. I also ordered a thali and a crab dish, both of which were absolutely delicious and the dessert tooo it’s new for me being a konkani
Overall, it was worth the visit. Great food, warm service, and a lovely atmosphere. I truly loved the experience and would definitely recommend this place.

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!
